provider: mcp.gd — MCP-native object storage for agents

free_tier.stated: Free: 10 GB storage, 10 GB/month traffic, 100 MB web upload. Paid Starter $5/mo: 100 GB storage, 100 GB/mo traffic, 10 GB web upload. Marketing claims 'up to 100GB per file' and 'no storage capacity cap'.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: 10 GB/month traffic on free. A hard egress meter, which is the real binding cap.

interface_detail: MCP over SSE (https://mcp.gd/mcp/sse) with OAuth 2.0 or bearer API token; REST/path API; 14 MCP tools
tooling: Claude.ai connector, Claude Desktop, `claude mcp add --transport sse mcp-gd`, curl with Bearer token
chaining: 10 GB free + 10 GB/month egress. The 'no storage cap, 100 GB per file' headline is contradicted by the 10 GB plan line on the same page.
limits_note: Free tier 10 GB storage / 10 GB monthly traffic / 100 MB web upload. The 100 GB per-file claim appears to be a platform limit, not a free-tier allowance.
reliability_note: Two numbers on the same page contradict: 'Up to 100GB per file … No storage capacity cap' in the feature list vs '10GB storage and 10GB/month traffic included at no cost' in the signup step. The free-tier number is the one with a price next to it, so it is the one to believe. Below the floor by 50x. Also the egress meter (10 GB/month) means it cannot serve the 500 GB-1 TB/day workload at all.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
